about: Every doctor row of docs/platform/config/spec.md section 11, one source for Rust and Node. doctor and check are the severity per consumer (fail or warn); detailSeverity replaces them for a finding whose detail names the key; fix is an id of `fixes` or null; `fixes` is also the order doctor applies them in (a copy of a key a legacy global file holds comes before a fresh machine file is created, so the user's own token is the one kept); needsAcknowledgement marks a fix that drops a note. Descriptions are English; no row echoes a value.

rows.description: A config file does not parse or breaks strict-config.
The value a source gives, alone or merged with the others, breaks a section schema, or a key sits in a scope that does not allow it.
config.yaml and config.json both exist in one scope.

A project or global file is still legacy JSON; run fgos config migrate (the global file: fgos config migrate --global --convert --machine-checked, after both key stages). Fails: every reader is on Config and no project keeps legacy JSON.
A @fgos:doc line differs from the schema and standard render. doctor warns, fgos config check fails.
A described key carries no @fgos:doc line.
A value in a file carries no @fgos:why line.
A value still carries the [migrate] reason; replace it with the real one.
A value equal to the standard; it holds nothing.
rows.needsAcknowledgementWhen: the key carries a why or a note

rows.description: An account pool or the gateway token sits in a config file. The destination decides: equal there is the state after the copy stage (the finishing verb removes the source); only the legacy global JSON file has a fix (the relocation reads that file); a project file has none.
The global, accounts or token file or ~/.fgos/private is wider than its mode.
A file directly under ~/.fgos outside private/ holds an account pool or a token.

A project or global file holds runner.capabilities.<x>.roles, .personas or .seats, which moved: roles and personas to runner.roles and runner.personas, seats to the workflow (a seat has no place in the config now). In the project file the fix moves each role and persona with its reason text (widened to every capability: runner.roles applies to all of them, and agreeing values from several capabilities merge) and drops the seats; the global file cannot hold the new tables, so there the fix only removes the keys and the finding says the taste belongs in the project file. When two places give one target different values, or the target holds another value, nothing is changed, no fix is offered and the finding names both paths for one fgos config patch (one transaction that unsets both old blocks and sets runner.roles.<role>; a single set or unset is refused while other retired keys remain).

The accounts file holds runner.providers.<provider>.accounts as an empty mapping, a leftover of the retired account inventory (the accounts live in runner.llmAccounts). The fix removes each empty accounts key, the provider entry when that was all it held, and runner.providers when no provider is left; a provider that still lists accounts is not touched here (the runner config refuses it by name).
A migration backup is older than the stale age and can be deleted.
~/.fgos/private or the gateway token file is missing or invalid.
